content: 1. Describe in detail the methods used to determine whether trachoma was a public health problem at baseline in each Evaluation Unit (EU). This includes, for any surveys conducted, the protocol followed and the sampling methodology employed. Additionally, if the status of any EU regarding trachoma as a public health problem was reassessed during the program, explain the reasons for and methods of reassessment. 2. In the accompanying data spreadsheet, provide baseline survey data (if collected) for trichiasis (Tab 1) and active trachoma (Tab 2) for each EU. Include maps to visually display these data and identify areas where baseline surveys were deemed unnecessary. 3. For trichiasis surgery, describe the selection, training, and certification processes for trichiasis surgeons. Detail the indications, contraindications, and techniques used for trichiasis surgery, as well as any non-surgical management methods employed. Explain the methods used for identifying individuals with trichiasis, the modes of delivery for trichiasis surgery (e.g., fixed sites, surgical camps, mobile teams), and whether adjunctive antibiotics were routinely administered during surgery. Include information on in-service supervision of surgeons, routine follow-up of operated patients, and any surgical audits conducted as part of the program. 4. In the accompanying data spreadsheet (Tab 1), provide data for each program year on the number of individuals (not eyes) who underwent trichiasis surgery in each EU. 5. For antibiotics, describe the antibiotic regimens used for community-level interventions against trachoma, including their indications and contraindications. Explain the methods used for community sensitization and antibiotic distribution, and report any significant challenges encountered, such as widespread refusal or serious adverse events. 6. In the accompanying data spreadsheet (Tab 2), provide data for each program year on the number of individuals who received antibiotics and the antibiotic coverage achieved in each EU. 7. For facial cleanliness promotion, describe the target groups (e.g., mothers of preschool-aged children, school-aged children), the types of personnel involved in promoting facial cleanliness, and the training and supervision provided to these personnel. Include details on the frequency of training and supervision, as well as the individuals or organizations responsible for delivering these activities. Specify whether these efforts were part of broader hygiene promotion initiatives. 8. In the accompanying data spreadsheet (Tab 2), identify the facial cleanliness activities delivered in each EU for each trachoma program year. 9. For environmental improvement, describe the activities undertaken to improve water availability and sanitation access in trachoma-endemic populations, including their intensity, scale, and the agencies responsible for implementation. Indicate whether there were any coordination or collaboration mechanisms between the trachoma program and other WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene) programs. 10. In the accompanying data spreadsheet (Tab 2), identify the environmental improvement interventions delivered in each EU for each trachoma program year. 11. For impact surveys, describe the timing and methods used, including the protocol followed and sampling methodology. In the accompanying data spreadsheet, provide impact survey data for trichiasis (Tab 1) and active trachoma (Tab 2) for each EU. 12. For pre-validation surveillance surveys, describe the timing and methods used, including the protocol followed and sampling methodology. In the accompanying data spreadsheet, provide pre-validation surveillance survey data for trichiasis (Tab 1) and active trachoma (Tab 2) for each EU. Include maps to visually display these data. 13. Briefly describe the current epidemiology of trachoma in bordering countries and comment on whether the disease in those countries poses a risk to the achievements of your program. Provide data on the current epidemiology of trachoma in bordering countries. 14. For post-validation surveillance, describe any national plans for post-validation trachoma surveillance, the provision of trichiasis surgical services until there are no longer any incident cases of trichiasis, and continued Ministry of Health engagement with other government ministries and partners responsible for WASH services. Ensure prioritization of EUs with the lowest levels of WASH service access. 15. Describe any special circumstances that have affected the program, such as stability or security issues in the country or immigration from other trachoma-endemic countries (e.g., nomadic populations, internally displaced persons, or refugees). 16. Briefly describe the human resources employed to implement the program and estimate the internal and external financial resources utilized. For example, mention specific financial support provided by organizations like Foundation X for trichiasis surgery in specific regions. 17. Include a bibliography of all data sources used to develop the dossier, such as Ministry of Health records, published papers, academic theses, and dissertations. Note that copies of unpublished documents may be requested by WHO. 18. Provide a list of all abbreviations used in the dossier, along with their definitions.
